subject: Skyhook / Paragon connector: technical validation & safety fallback review
messages:

Cc: Skyhook Eng Ops <engops@skyhook-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connector validation: Paragon -> Redwood (safety & fallback questions)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the initial architecture session last week. Skyhook is helping Paragon Analytics integrate their inference orchestration layer into Redwood Dedicated. Before we move to a sandbox POC, Paragon's security team has two asks: a) confirm how the connector handles streaming failures and model fallback so they can map to their SLA; b) an explicit safety-check run that exercises disallowed-output fallbacks (we need an example report).

Attached is a short sample trace from their internal gateway showing abrupt 502s when the KV cache times out (trace-aug-2.log). Can you point me to the right person for the technical validation and a proposed timeline for a short safety run?

Appreciate it — Jordan

--
Jordan Lee
Integration Lead, Paragon Analytics
jordan.lee@paragon-analytics.com
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@paragon-analytics.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector validation: Paragon -> Redwood (safety & fallback questions)

Jordan —

Thanks for the trace. We'll own the technical validation. Quick plan below:

1) Safety smoke run (2 business days) — run our safety harness against a small set of Paragon prompts and capture fallback behavior (explicit deny, model-switch, or sanitization). We will produce a short "safety-test-report.pdf" with examples and timelines.
2) Failure-mode tests (1 day) — synthetic 502s and KV cache expirations to validate graceful degradation: automatic fallback to stateless model variant, retry + backoff, and request-level caching behavior.
3) Canary & perf (2 days) — run a constrained traffic canary in Redwood Dedicated sandbox with target SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for token generation at median sequence lengths.

Sergio will run the architecture checklist and Aditya will own the canary plan. Can you confirm a sandbox dataset (anonymized) and whether Paragon requires us to hit their test endpoints for TLS mutual auth?

Proposed kickoff: Wed 11 Aug, 10:00 PT (30m).

Cheers,
Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@paragon-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector validation: Paragon -> Redwood (safety & fallback questions)

Jordan / Naomi —

I've gone through the sample trace. A few items from the architecture checklist I want confirmed before we start tests:

- TLS and auth: do you require mTLS? If yes, supply cert bundle and allowed CNs.
- KMS/HSM: will Paragon bring their key material, or should we use Redwood KMS (customer-key namespace)?
- Session affinity: how long do you expect KV cache pins to be retained on the gateway? Our KV-sharding means longer pins affect cache hit ratios and can push latencies up under heavy concurrency.
- Model variants: what is the acceptable fallback chain? (e.g., full-precision model -> quantized variant -> stateless small model)

For the safety harness I'll validate the ACLs and the sanitization layer. We'll also capture per-token debug traces so we can reproduce denial decisions.

Attach: connector-reference-design.yaml (expected config for the POC), and I'll add a short checklist to the drive link Naomi shared.

Sergio
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@paragon-analytics.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector validation: Paragon -> Redwood (safety & fallback questions)

Thanks Sergio — answers inline: 

- mTLS: yes, Paragon requires mTLS for test endpoints (we'll send cert bundle this afternoon).
- KMS: Paragon will use their KMS in the sandbox (customer-owned keys) — they asked for a KMS audit flow and access scoping.
- Session affinity: gateway retains KV pins for up to 45s by default; can be tuned.
- Fallback chain: Paragon is comfortable with the following for safety-critical paths: primary high-accuracy model (fp16) -> quantized 8-bit variant -> small stateless model with content-filtering. They need documented SLOs for each step.

Attaching an anonymized request sample and a short log excerpt. We'll join Wed 11 Aug at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Jordan
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@paragon-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Canary plan & pass/fail criteria for Paragon connector POC

Team — following today's kickoff, here is the canary run plan (summary):

Scope:
- 48-hour constrained traffic canary in the Redwood Dedicated sandbox (single GPU pool).
- Synthetic mix: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256), 10% long (>256).

Metrics & pass/fail:
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms (generation time per request) across median sequence length set.
- Error budget: <= 0.5% 5xx responses over 48h.
- Fallback correctness: for 20 seeded safety triggers, at least 95% must result in documented fallback behavior (deny/sanitize/model-switch) and have a recorded debug trace.
- KV cache resilience: simulate 5 intermittent cache eviction events and verify downstream retries/backoff do not exceed 5s tail latency spike and all requests succeed within 30s.

Runbook highlights:
- Start canary at 10:00 PT with traffic ramp to 15% of target within 30 minutes.
- Monitor canary dashboard link and abort on any p95 > 600ms or error rate > 2%.

I'll push the canary config to the shared drive and tag the HubSpot deal once we have a clean safety report. I'll also attach a sample prom-script and the metrics screenshot after the run.

- Aditya
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
